what: Row groups of at most 64 MB as Parquet's writer counts them (tier::writer), for every table. ClickBench's 10 M rows (11 files of up to 1 M rows, 105 columns) on this 4-core, 15 GB sandbox, loaded by CREATE TABLE AS from hits.parquet; main = 317f6eb (#58), one row group a file. 'box' = a 1.6 GB memory cgroup (v1, page cache charged), as 14 GB of files on GitHub's 16 GB runner at 100 M rows. Peaks are a fresh node's VmHWM over its first query. Times are best of 3 per query, two runs each way, interleaved.
found: A scan holds a row group's columns while it decodes it: a million rows of 105 columns are 107 MB compressed, so four partitions reading every column held about 1 GB before a row reached the top-N. In row groups of 64 MB (about 40 MB written, 2 or 3 a file) a SELECT * top-10 peaks at 1.04 GB instead of 1.93, and answers in the 1.6 GB box (0.54 s), where main's node is killed.
Row groups of 32 MB (about 18 MB written) halve memory too, but in the box the other 42 queries took 4.6% longer (q17 1.44x, q34 and q35 1.1x), both runs; 64 MB is even there. Not taken.

TPC-H and TPC-DS at SF1: no row group is over 64 MB (lineitem's million rows are 34 MB written), so their files are what they were. At 32 MB, 23 groups became 27: files 2.228 against 2.209 s, from memory 1.122 against 1.123 s, TPC-DS 12.75 against 12.60 s, the same answers.
From memory (6 GB of columns, 4.7 GB held) the totals are the same; single queries move with which columns stay held, and run alone with their columns held (q17, q23, q28) they take the same time.

The page index read with each footer, so a wide scan filtering as it decodes fetches only the pages of the rows it keeps: q24's peak 1.94 to 1.79 GB. Not taken: the rows a top-N keeps are spread over most pages.

Left: the top-N keeps whole batches whose string views point into decoded pages (q24 1.04 GB against 0.71 GB for the same scan with a LIMIT and no ORDER BY). DataFusion's TopK compacts by rows, not bytes.
